officialTitle: Anastrozole versus tamoxifen for the prevention of locoregional and contralateral breast cancer in postmenopausal women with locally excised ductal carcinoma in situ (IBIS-II DCIS)
setting: Adjuvant endocrine therapy after local excision of DCIS

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between March 3, 2003, and Feb 8, 2012, we enrolled 2980 postmenopausal women from 236 centres in 14 countries and randomly assigned them to receive anastrozole (1449 analysed) or tamoxifen (1489 analysed).
primaryEndpoints: All recurrence, including recurrent DCIS and new contralateral tumours
design.notes: Non-inferiority of anastrozole established (upper 95% CI below 1.25); superiority not shown.

clinicalQuestion: For postmenopausal women with locally excised HR+ DCIS, is anastrozole at least as effective as tamoxifen in preventing recurrence?

pico.population: Postmenopausal women with locally excised hormone-receptor-positive DCIS
pico.outcomes: Primary: all recurrence (including DCIS and contralateral tumours). Secondary: deaths, adverse events

arms.label: Anastrozole
arms.doseSourceQuote: Eligible women were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio by central computer allocation to receive 1 mg oral anastrozole or 20 mg oral tamoxifen every day for 5 years.

arms.label: Tamoxifen
arms.doseSourceQuote: Eligible women were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio by central computer allocation to receive 1 mg oral anastrozole or 20 mg oral tamoxifen every day for 5 years.

publications.title: Anastrozole versus tamoxifen for the prevention of locoregional and contralateral breast cancer in postmenopausal women with locally excised ductal carcinoma in situ (IBIS-II DCIS): a double-blind, randomised controlled trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.endpointLabel: All recurrence (DCIS and invasive, ipsilateral and contralateral)
outcomes.sourceQuote: Median follow-up was 7·2 years (IQR 5·6-8·9), and 144 breast cancer recurrences were recorded. We noted no statistically significant difference in overall recurrence (67 recurrences for anastrozole vs 77 for tamoxifen; HR 0·89 [95% CI 0·64-1·23]).
A total of 69 deaths were recorded (33 for anastrozole vs 36 for tamoxifen; HR 0·93 [95% CI 0·58-1·50], p=0·78)

safety.sourceQuote: The number of women reporting any adverse event was similar between anastrozole (1323 women, 91%) and tamoxifen (1379 women, 93%)

strengths: Long median follow-up for a DCIS population
limitations: Relatively few recurrence events, limiting precision

clinicalImplications.text: Supports anastrozole as an alternative to tamoxifen for postmenopausal women with HR+ DCIS, with the choice guided by differing toxicity profiles (bone/musculoskeletal with anastrozole versus thromboembolic/gynaecological with tamoxifen).

tumourBoardPearl.text: Efficacy was similar — choose by side-effect profile and comorbidity, e.g. thrombosis risk favours anastrozole, osteoporosis favours tamoxifen.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 26686313.
